**Wire verb `genes map-residues`**: Map a residue of one protein to the residue of another protein in the same column of Ensembl Compara's gene-tree alignment, or say why there is none, for a batch of queries.

- [`ComparaGeneTreeAlignment.Load`](https://github.com/smith-chem-wisc/mzLib/blob/cc67b7a29/mzLib/UsefulProteomicsDatabases/Ensembl/ComparaGeneTreeAlignment.cs) in `mzLib/UsefulProteomicsDatabases/Ensembl/ComparaGeneTreeAlignment.cs` at mzLib `cc67b7a2`

# Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Unit | Range | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `alignment` (wire `--alignment`) | `path` | required | — | — | Compara's peptide alignments of its gene trees, emf/ensembl-compara/homologies/Compara.RELEASE.protein\_COLLECTION.aa.fasta.gz (plain or .gz): one gapped multiple alignment per tree, as FASTA, separated by a // line. Read with ComparaGeneTreeAlignment.Load, which keeps only the canonical proteins of the genes kept from gene-trees, and checks every row's characters and width whether it is kept or not. 908 MB compressed for protein\_default in release 116. |
| `gene_trees` (wire `--gene-trees`) | `path` | required | — | — | Compara's gene-tree membership dump, COLLECTION.GeneTree\_content.default.eRELEASE.txt.gz (plain or .gz), read with ComparaGeneTreeContent.Load. It names each gene's tree and its canonical protein (the row flagged Y), which is the only protein of the gene the alignment holds. |
| `species` (wire `--species`) | `string[]` | absent | — | `>= 0 lines; each exactly three tab-separated fields` | Read from stdin (not an option), first: one line per species, the species' Ensembl production name (homo\_sapiens), a tab, gtf or gene-set, a tab, and the path, exactly as genes orthology reads them. gtf is an Ensembl primary-assembly GTF, read with EnsemblGeneSet.LoadGtf; gene-set is the compact table mzLib's EnsemblGeneSetWriter makes from one, read with EnsemblGeneSetReader.Load. Their only use is ComparaGeneTreeContent.Load's restrictTo: only the genes in them are kept, and so only their canonical proteins. None (the stdin starts with --): mzLib's default, restrictTo null, keeps every gene in the gene-tree file and every canonical protein in the alignment, millions for the vertebrate collection, and a caveat says so. A species listed twice, a kind other than gtf or gene-set, or a missing file is a usage error. |
| `queries` (wire `--queries`) | `string[]` | required | — | `>= 1 line; each exactly three tab-separated fields` | Read from stdin (not an option), after a line holding only --: one query per line, the source protein's Ensembl stable id, a tab, a 1-based residue position in it, a tab, and the target protein's id (ENSP00000269305, 15, ENSMUSP00000104298). One row per query, in input order, duplicates included. The position is parsed as an integer and passed to MapResidue unchecked; the bridge does not compare it with the protein's length. |
| `proteins` (wire `--proteins`) | `flag` | `false` | — | — | Also return the kept proteins (ComparaGeneTreeAlignment.Proteins: id, alignment, tree and ungapped sequence), so a protein's Ensembl sequence can be aligned to a UniProt sequence with proteins align without a second file. Absent: proteins is null. |

# Returns

Top-level fields:

| Field | Type | Unit | Null? | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `alignment` | `object` | — | never | The alignment file and what was kept from it (typed under result.tables.alignment). |
| `gene_trees` | `object` | — | never | The gene-tree file and what was kept from it, the same fields as genes orthology's gene\_trees (typed under result.tables.gene\_trees). |
| `gene_sets` | `map<string,object>` | — | never | Species to its gene set, in ordinal order of species, each with genes resolve's gene\_set fields (typed under result.tables.gene\_sets). Empty when no species lines were given. |
| `row_count` | `int` | queries | never | Rows: the queries, one each. |
| `outcome_counts` | `map<string,int>` | queries | never | Outcome to queries with it, every ComparaColumnOutcome in mzLib's declaration order, zeros included. |
| `columns` (wire `column_names`) | `string[]` | — | never | The mapping table's columns in order. |
| `columns` | `table` | — | never | Column name to one value per query, in input order. |
| `proteins_included` | `bool` | — | never | Whether --proteins was given. |
| `proteins` | `object` | — | yes: --proteins was not given | {row\_count, column\_names, columns}: one row per kept protein, in ordinal order of protein id (typed under result.tables.proteins). |
| `caveats` | `string[]` | — | never | This call's traps: gene trees read unrestricted (every gene kept), an alignment and gene-tree file named for different releases or for none, queries naming a protein the alignment did not keep. |

Per-row fields (one value per record, in `columns` or each list entry):

| Field | Type | Unit | Null? | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `source_protein_id` | `string` | — | never | The query's source protein id, as given. |
| `position` | `int` | — | never | The query's 1-based residue position in the source protein, as given. |
| `target_protein_id` | `string` | — | never | The query's target protein id, as given. |
| `outcome` | `string` | — | never | mzLib's ComparaColumnOutcome name, verbatim: Aligned (the target has a residue in the source residue's column), GapInTarget (the target has a gap there: no residue corresponds, never the nearest one), DifferentAlignments (the two proteins are in different gene trees, so the alignment says nothing about them), SourceNotInAlignment or TargetNotInAlignment (that protein was not kept: not in the file, not a canonical protein, or outside the gene sets). Exactly one per query. |
| `column` | `int` | — | yes: the two proteins do not share an alignment (DifferentAlignments, SourceNotInAlignment or TargetNotInAlignment) | The source residue's 1-based column in the gene tree's alignment. Set for Aligned and GapInTarget. |
| `target_position` | `int` | — | yes: the outcome is not Aligned | The 1-based position of the target's residue in that column, in the target's ungapped sequence. |
| `target_residue` | `string` | — | yes: the outcome is not Aligned | The target's residue there, one letter as the alignment writes it. It may differ from the source's residue: a column pairs homologous positions, not identical ones. |

# Errors

| Kind | mzLibRust returns | When |
|---|---|---|
| `usage` | [`MzLibError::Usage`](crate::MzLibError::Usage) | --alignment or --gene-trees missing or given without a value; a value after --proteins |
| `usage` | [`MzLibError::Usage`](crate::MzLibError::Usage) | no line holding only -- on stdin, or no queries after it; a species line that is not species, tab, gtf or gene-set, tab, path; a species listed twice; a query that is not three tab-separated fields, or whose position is not an integer |
| `usage` | [`MzLibError::Usage`](crate::MzLibError::Usage) | a GTF, gene-set table, gene-trees file or alignment that does not exist (checked before any input is read) |
| `usage` | [`MzLibError::Usage`](crate::MzLibError::Usage) | mzLib's MapResidue refused a query's position as outside the source protein (ArgumentOutOfRangeException): 0, negative, or past its last residue. The message names the query and quotes mzLib, which gives the protein's length. The whole call fails on the first such query, in input order, and no row is returned. A source protein that is not kept is an outcome, SourceNotInAlignment, checked before the position. |
| `correctness` | [`MzLibError::Bridge`](crate::MzLibError::Bridge) | a file mzLib's reader refuses (InvalidDataException, naming file and line): in the alignment, a sequence line before any header, an empty header, a character that is not a letter, \* or -, rows of different widths, an empty alignment, a kept protein twice, or an alignment whose kept proteins belong to two gene trees; in the gene-tree file, a row without four cells, a flag other than Y or N, or a kept gene in two trees or without exactly one canonical protein; a GTF gene row without gene\_id |
| `service_unavailable` | [`MzLibError::ServiceUnavailable`](crate::MzLibError::ServiceUnavailable) | never returned by this verb |

Any call can also fail on the way to mzLib or back, whatever the verb: [`MzLibError::BridgeNotFound`](crate::MzLibError::BridgeNotFound), [`MzLibError::Timeout`](crate::MzLibError::Timeout), [`MzLibError::Protocol`](crate::MzLibError::Protocol) or [`MzLibError::Io`](crate::MzLibError::Io).

# Caveats

- A column pairs positions that Compara's alignment puts together, which is homology, not identity: the target residue may be a different amino acid, so check target\_residue before carrying a modification across (a phosphosite on S is not a site on A).
- Only each gene's canonical protein is in the alignment (the gene-tree row flagged Y). A query naming another isoform's Ensembl id is SourceNotInAlignment or TargetNotInAlignment, never mapped through the canonical one. To start from a UniProt position, align the UniProt sequence to the canonical Ensembl protein with proteins align first, then map, then align the target's canonical protein to its UniProt sequence: three steps, each of which can meet a gap.
- A gap is GapInTarget, never the nearest residue: no residue of the target sits in that column.
- DifferentAlignments means the two proteins are in different gene trees, so this alignment says nothing about them. It does not say the genes are not homologous, nor that they are orthologs when they share one: a tree holds paralogs as well, so read orthology from genes orthology.
- mzLib's MapResidue throws for a position outside the source protein instead of returning an outcome, so one such query fails the whole call, and the bridge does not check lengths for it. Keep positions inside each source protein; --proteins gives each kept protein's sequence.
- mzLib does not compare the alignment's release with the gene-tree file's. Use the two files of one release: a gene's canonical protein and its tree can change between releases. The envelope reports the release each file name carries, and a caveat says when they differ or one is absent.
- Every input is read whole, and the alignment keeps only the canonical proteins of the genes kept, so give the species' gene sets: with none, every gene in the gene-tree file is kept (millions for the vertebrate collection), and so every canonical protein of the alignment.
